speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you tell me what happened right before you lost consciousness, and did you experience any shaking or jerking movements during the event?

REQUEST TEST: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP)
REQUEST TEST: Toxicology Screen

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing those results; they appear to be within normal limits. Since the metabolic, blood, and toxicology screens are clear, did you experience any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath leading up to the fainting spell? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision or hearing prior to losing consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you feel any lightheadedness, dizziness, or warmth spreading through your body right before you passed out? Also, has this ever happened to you before, or do you have a history of heart disease or high blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasovagal Syncope secondary to micturition syncope.

REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram (to rule out structural heart disease despite the clinical picture).
